arguments.spec:
# Encrypted Backup and Restore — card plan specification

Produce `plan/cards.json`: a dependency-linked set of implementation-team cards discharging every obligation below.
This is a planning deliverable only — no application code, docs, or tests are written by this graph.

- OBL-01: A snapshot must record every regular file's path, size, mode and modification time, skipping sockets,
  fifos and device nodes without failing the run. [module: src/backup/snapshot.js]
- OBL-02: A snapshot must detect a file that changed while being read and re-read it, bounded, before failing that
  path. [module: src/backup/snapshot.js]
- OBL-03: Chunking must be content-defined so inserting a byte near the start of a large file re-uploads only the
  chunks around the insertion. [module: src/backup/chunker.js]
- OBL-04: Chunk boundaries must be reproducible: identical on every machine and every run. [module:
  src/backup/chunker.js]
- OBL-05: Each chunk must be encrypted with a key derived from the passphrase and a per-repository salt, never the
  passphrase alone. [module: src/backup/encrypt.js]
- OBL-06: Encryption must be authenticated: altered ciphertext or header must fail to decrypt rather than yield
  wrong plaintext. [module: src/backup/encrypt.js]
- OBL-07: The chunk store must be content-addressed; writing a chunk that already exists must be a no-op. [module:
  src/backup/store.js]
- OBL-08: The store must survive an interrupted write: a partial chunk must be invisible to readers and
  reclaimable on the next run. [module: src/backup/store.js]
- OBL-09: Restore must verify every chunk against its content address before use, and name the first chunk that
  fails. [module: src/restore/verify.js]
- OBL-10: A dry-run restore must report exactly which files it would write, which it would skip, and why, without
  touching the filesystem. [module: src/restore/verify.js]
- OBL-11: Restore must refuse to overwrite an existing file unless told to, and restore recorded modes and
  modification times. [module: src/restore/apply.js]
- OBL-12: An interrupted restore must be resumable: rerunning it completes the remaining files without redoing the
  finished ones. [module: src/restore/apply.js]
- OBL-13: The scheduler must support hourly, daily and weekly cadence, skipping a run rather than stacking two
  overlapping backups. [module: src/cli/schedule.js]
- OBL-14: The restore drill must be documented as a numbered procedure, including how to verify the result.
  (documentation-only) [module: docs/runbook-restore.md]
- OBL-15: The retention policy must be written down: how long each cadence is kept, what prunes it, who approves
  an exception. (documentation-only) [module: docs/retention-policy.md]
- OBL-16: The threat model must state what the tool protects against, what it does not, and where the passphrase
  is trusted. (documentation-only) [module: docs/threat-model.md]
- OBL-17: The status report must show last successful backup, store size, chunk count and the age of the oldest
  unverified chunk. [module: src/report/status.js]
- OBL-18: The operator guide must document every exit code the tool can return and the action each one calls for.
  (documentation-only) [module: docs/operator-guide.md]

## Non-goals
Cloud storage backends, multi-machine deduplication, a GUI and continuous replication are all out of scope (carried
over verbatim from input/specification.md; this card plan does not revisit them).
arguments.plan:
Two cards, chained:
1. `draft-card-plan` reads input/specification.md and writes the complete plan/cards.json, grouping every pair of
   obligations that share one `[module: path]` tag onto a single card, and splitting each documentation-only
   obligation onto its own not-testable card.
2. `verify-plan-coverage` depends on it, re-reads the file fresh (never trusts the prior card's summary), hand-verifies
   the obligation union is exactly OBL-01 through OBL-18 with none missing or duplicated, and runs the real
   `npm test` before confirming `complete:true`.
